To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UCP1 down-regulates the lipolytically important hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL), lowers the expression of Gs and Gz subunits and reduces the stimulatory effect of noradrenalin on lipolysis.
UCP1 overexpression in adipocytes reduces noradrenaline-stimulated lipolysis and the expression of hormone sensitive lipase, and that this is associated with changes at the G protein level.
the lipolytic effect and signalling of the sympathetic nervous system in adipose tissue is modulated by the energy status of adipocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of energy homeostasis by UCP1 in adipose tissue.
the role of UCPs in the regulation of lipolysis in vivo.
a new mechanism of energy homeostasis, and it may be important in understanding the role of UCPs in energy balance and obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UCP1 in adipocytes lowers the ATP level and the lipolytic effect by catecholamine, but also changes the expression of G-proteins, thus tending to compensate for the lowered lipolysis.
the expression of UCP1 in adipocytes leads to a reduction of the lipolytic effect exerted by noradrenalines in subcutaneous adipose tissue, but not in epididymal adipose tissue.
UCP1 expression affects the energy status of adipocytes, and that this affects lipolysis and the noradrenaline response in adipose tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UCP1 overexpression in fat tissue of aP2-UCP1 transgenic mice results in a reduction of the noradrenaline induced lipolysis.

the uncoupling proteins, UCP1 and UCP3, have a negative impact on the lipolytic effect and the cAMP level in adipose tissue, and this effect depends on the expression level of the UCPs and on the depot.
UCP1 over-expression in white adipocytes impairs lipolysis by lowering the ATP/ADp ratio and by altering the levels of G-proteins that are important in noradrenaline-stimulated lipolysis.

UCP1 can be considered as a potential target for the treatment of obesity and its related metabolic complications.
